correctness.rationale: By theta(y)~y, q<=2 log N for all sufficiently large odd N. The binary half-divisor-sum certificate proves 2^b q is Zumkeller for all b>=a. Every p<=N/2 in the reduced class p=N mod B but not mod Bq has N-p=2^(a+t)q*m0, gcd(m0,2^(a+t)q)=1. Multiplying a Zumkeller base by coprime m0 preserves equal divisor partition. Thus R(N)>=pi(N/2;B,N)-pi(N/2;Bq,N). Both moduli are uniformly <=O(log^3 N) and phi(Bq)=q phi(B). Uniform Siegel–Walfisz for each gives the (1-1/q) Li/phi(B) main term plus negligible relative error, and phi(B)<q^2<=4log^2 N gives the cubic logarithmic lower bound. This is an ineffective eventually-large-N theorem, not a finite-exception census or exact asymptotic for all representations.
residual_risks: Finite verification alone does not establish universal quantifiers; correctness rests on the fully reconstructed proof.

value.rationale: The original prime-plus-Zumkeller conjecture is a natural additive-number-theory question. Replacing a square-modulus sieve by one residue class modulo B minus a single refinement modulo Bq genuinely improves the worst-case bound by two powers of log N and yields an exact admissible residue-density fraction within the local sieve; this is not a constant-only gain or finite table.

final_claim: Uniformly over sufficiently large odd N, choosing q as the least missing odd prime, a minimal q<=2^(a+1)-1 and B=2^a q, the count R(N) of prime p<=N/2 with Zumkeller N-p exceeds (1-1/q+o(1)) Li(N/2)/phi(B), hence R(N)>>N/(log N)^3.
